tip: With reciprocal si and essere, the past participle agrees with the subject: incontrati ends in -i for a masculine or mixed group.
Come se (as if) always takes the subjunctive: come se niente fosse successo, never è successo.
The future perfect can express a guess about the past: avrà dimenticato means 'he must have forgotten', not a real future.
Magari plus the imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish: magari il tempo passasse, if only time passed.
Trapassato prossimo (had done) = imperfect of avere plus the participle: avevano costruito, they had built.
For real, likely conditions, se takes the present indicative: se trovi, not a subjunctive. Save the subjunctive for hypotheticals.
Unreal present 'if': se plus the imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional: se sapessi guidare, affitterei.
Pure after a command softens it to 'go ahead, feel free': chiedi pure, just ask.
Dimenticarsi is followed by di before the thing forgotten: dimenticarsi del compleanno, forget about the birthday.
Volere che forces the subjunctive: volevano che partissimo, never volevano che partivamo.
Stesso after a time word means 'this very': domani stesso, tomorrow itself, no later.
Dell' is di plus the article, the partitive for 'some': c'è dell'acqua, there's some water.
Futuro anteriore marks an action finished before a future point: avrò consegnato, I will have handed it in.
Object pronouns attach to the end of an infinitive: ringraziare plus ti becomes ringraziarti, to thank you.
Il before a weekday means 'every': il sabato, on Saturdays as a habit; drop il for one specific Saturday.
Italian keeps the double negative: non volesse smettere mai literally says 'not... never', meaning would never stop.
Object pronouns sit before a conjugated verb: lo visiteremmo, we'd visit it, not visiteremmo lo.
Così before an adverb or adjective means 'so': costasse così tanto, cost so much.
Unreal past 'if': se plus the pluperfect subjunctive, then the past conditional: se avessi dimenticato, saresti partito.
Italian often uses the present for a certain near future: se mi chiami, vengo, means I'll come.
Quello che means 'what' in the sense of 'the thing that': quello che hai fatto, what you did.
Prima di is followed by the infinitive, not a conjugated verb: prima di litigare, before quarreling.
Poiché means 'since' or 'because', giving a reason, and takes the indicative: poiché era pieno, since it was full.
Weather uses fare: fa bello means the weather is nice, literally 'it makes nice'.
